AbstractText.Label: INTRODUCTION
AbstractText.content: Thermal ablation of tumors by Nd:YAG laser has been growing as a multidisciplinary subspecialty defined as laser-induced thermal therapy (LITT), and has been increasingly accepted as a minimally invasive method for palliation of advanced or recurrent cancer. Previous studies have shown that adjuvant chemotherapy can potentiate laser thermal ablation of tumors leading to improved palliation in advanced cancer patients.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: Evaluate nephrotoxicity by early markers of renal function in treating head and neck cancer using intra-tumor injections of cisplatin combined with laser-induced thermal therapy (CDDP-LITT).

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Nine patients with recurrent head and neck tumors were treated by CDDP-LITT in order to determine nephrotoxicity related to this synergistic association. Among the tests requested to detect early were creatinine, magnesium, creatinine clearance, serum urea-BUN, type I urine, and proteinuria at 24 hours.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Twelve recurrent tumors in nine patients were treated by CDDP-LITT. Pain was the major complaint (four patients), while other symptoms included dysphagia, dyspnea, bleeding, and difficulties in chewing. Fifteen laser procedures were performed and maximal CDDP dose was 50 mg. None of the markers for nephrotoxicity showed changes at these levels of CDDP intra-tumor injections.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: This initial experience with (CDDP-LITT) indicates both safety and therapeutic potential for palliation of advanced head and neck cancer. However, safety and feasibility must be confirmed by longer follow-up and further escalation of CDDP doses in a Phase I study to determine maximum tolerated dose (MTD) and demonstrate tangible benefits for patients.
